title: Citi Recommends Buying the Dip in Memory Stocks as AI Cycle Gains Momentum
excerpt: Citi believes the recent sell-off in memory chip stocks presents a buying opportunity, arguing that the artificial intelligence-driven memory cycle is still...
content_html:
Citi believes the recent sell-off in memory chip stocks presents a buying opportunity, arguing that the artificial intelligence-driven memory cycle is still in its early phases and could ultimately exceed the industry's previous boom between 2001 and 2007.

The bank says the current environment shares many similarities with the long NAND expansion seen during the early 2000s, when products such as MP3 players and digital cameras transformed demand and flash memory steadily replaced older storage technologies.

Recent Pullback Follows Powerful Rally

Memory chip makers have retreated sharply after posting substantial gains earlier this year. Shares of Micron (NASDAQ:MU), Samsung Electronics Co Ltd (USOTC:SSNHZ) and SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) have each fallen by more than 20% from recent highs as investors became concerned about elevated valuations and the sustainability of AI-related capital spending.

Despite that weakness, Citi believes the long-term investment case remains intact.

The bank said the current cycle "is likely to outperform the '01–'07 upcycle given that AI demand is driving both DRAM and NAND demand."

Long-Term Contracts Reinforce Demand Outlook

According to Citi, one of the strongest indicators that the current upcycle still has room to run is the increasing use of long-term agreements.

Customers are reportedly signing contracts lasting between three and five years, suggesting confidence that demand will remain elevated for longer than many investors originally anticipated.

The bank believes these agreements improve long-term earnings visibility across the sector.

HBM Supply Constraints Continue to Shape AI Infrastructure

Citi also highlighted the ongoing shortage of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which it expects will influence how artificial intelligence infrastructure evolves.

Rather than concentrating computing power into a smaller number of GPUs with very high HBM content, AI developers are increasingly expected to adopt a "scale-out" strategy by deploying larger numbers of GPUs with lower HBM capacity per chip.

Even so, Citi forecasts that overall HBM capacity within AI systems will continue expanding rapidly.

The bank estimates total HBM capacity per AI system will increase by 434%, rising from 20.7 terabytes to 110.6 terabytes as the number of GPUs per system grows from 72 to 576.

Citi Remains Positive on SK Hynix

The bank also pointed to comments from SK Hynix during its second-quarter earnings call, where management indicated it is evaluating additional shareholder return initiatives.

content_html_zh:
花旗认为，最近内存芯片股票的抛售提供了买入机会，认为人工智能驱动的内存周期仍处于早期阶段，最终可能超过该行业 2001 年至 2007 年期间的繁荣时期。

该银行表示，当前的环境与 2000 年代初期的 NAND 长期扩张有许多相似之处，当时 MP3 播放器和数码相机等产品改变了需求，闪存稳步取代了旧的存储技术。

强劲反弹后近期回调

内存芯片制造商在今年早些时候大幅上涨后，已大幅回落。 由于投资者开始担心估值上升和人工智能相关资本支出的可持续性，美光科技 (NASDAQ:MU)、三星电子有限公司 (USOTC:SSNHZ) 和 SK 海力士 (NASDAQ:SKHY) 的股价均较近期高点下跌超过 20%。

尽管存在这种疲软，但花旗认为长期投资理由仍然完好无损。

该银行表示，鉴于人工智能需求正在推动 DRAM 和 NAND 需求，当前周期的表现可能会优于 01 年至 07 年的上行周期。

长期合同增强了需求前景

花旗表示，当前上升周期仍有运行空间的最有力指标之一是长期协议的使用增加。

据报道，客户正在签署为期三到五年的合同，这表明人们有信心需求将保持高位的时间比许多投资者最初预期的要长。

该银行认为，这些协议提高了整个行业的长期盈利可见性。

HBM 供应限制继续影响人工智能基础设施

花旗还强调了高带宽内存（HBM）的持续短缺，预计这将影响人工智能基础设施的发展。

AI 开发人员越来越期望采用“横向扩展”策略，部署更多数量的 GPU（每芯片 HBM 容量较低），而不是将计算能力集中到数量较少、HBM 含量非常高的 GPU 中。

即便如此，花旗预测人工智能系统内的整体 HBM 能力将继续快速扩张。

该银行预计，随着每个系统的 GPU 数量从 72 个增加到 576 个，每个 AI 系统的 HBM 总容量将增加 434%，从 20.7 TB 增加到 110.6 TB。

花旗仍看好 SK 海力士

该银行还提到了 SK 海力士在第二季度财报电话会议上的评论，管理层表示正在评估额外的股东回报计划。
